key_insight: HamQASBench reframes quantum architecture search evaluation around Hamiltonian structure, exposing hidden failure modes that energy-only benchmarks miss.
engineering_relevance: It gives quantum engineers a more diagnostic way to compare QAS methods by linking circuit design quality to entanglement, fidelity, and Hamiltonian complexity.
method: Groups 11 molecules into five structural tiers using Pauli-basis, computational-basis, and ground-state entanglement fingerprints.
Extracts minimal critical circuits post hoc to match each tier’s structural requirements.
Evaluates QAS methods with energy accuracy plus per-qubit entanglement and pairwise state fidelity.
evidence_signal: The benchmark studies five QAS methods across four paradigms and reveals distinct failure modes such as over-parameterization, degeneracy-driven commitment, representation bottlenecks, routing failures, and scalability limits.
watch_item: Because the benchmark relies on derived structural tiers and post-hoc circuit extraction, its diagnostic conclusions may depend on the chosen fingerprinting and simplification procedure.
paper_title: HamQASBench: A Hamiltonian-Informed Diagnostic Benchmark for Evaluating Quantum Architecture Search
